Uniform Title: *Mahālakṣmīpūjāvidhiḥ* Manuscript: NGMCP 1696/2310 Reel No.: B 375/47 Description: Ritual manual on the worship of Mahālakṣmī.
Notes: Data entered by the staff of Muktabodha under the direction of Mark S. G. Dyczkowski. Revision 0: April 28, 2017.
Publication country: India.

1a) Oṃ, salutations to the goddess Śrī Mahālakṣmī. Salutations to Brahmā. Oṃ, salutations to the gurus. Oṃ, salutations to Gaṇapati. Oṃ, salutations to the chosen deities (iṣṭadevatās). Having thus performed the worship and prostration to the gurus: Oṃ, salutations to the foundation (ādhāraśakti). Oṃ, salutations to the armor (kavaca) of devotion. Holding a single-stemmed flower, one should then offer the arghya to the Sun. From today onwards, for the purpose of commencing the vow of Śrī Mahālakṣmī, [this is offered] to the Sun, the Great Radiance (vṛhadbhānu).

Salutation! Again, from the beginning: Obeisance, obeisance again and again! To the venerable Mahākālī, together with her limbs, her attendants, and her retinue, and to the world-protectors headed by Indra—for the purpose of commencing the vow of the venerable Mahālakṣmī—come, svāhā! One should begin the ritual placement (*nyāsa*): *Oṃ*, salutation to the weapon (*astra*). [This is] the purification of the hands.

1b) Oṃ, salutation to the little finger (kaniṣṭhā). Oṃ, salutation to the nose (nāsikā). Oṃ, salutation to the middle finger (madhyamā). Oṃ, salutation to the ring finger (taryanī). Oṃ, salutation to the thumb (aṅguṣṭha). Oṃ, salutation to the backs of the hands (karapṛṣṭha). Thus is the *karanyāsa* (hand-assignment). Oṃ, salutation to the heart (hṛdaya). Oṃ, salutation to the head (śiras). Oṃ, salutation to the crest-lock (śikhā). Oṃ, salutation to the armor (kavaca). Oṃ, salutation to the eyes (netra). Oṃ, salutation to the weapon (astra). Thus is the *aṅganyāsa* (limb-assignment). With this, perform the worship of the *arghapātra* (offering vessel). [Make] three *añjali*s (salutations with joined palms).
Having held [it]: Oṃ, O World-Conqueror, O Supreme Lakṣmī, O Supreme Goddess, O Mistress of Kamala, O Great Lakṣmī of the Splendor of the Lotus, grant me boons; svāhā!

May all that pertains to the worship— invocation, installation, presence, absorption, bathing, water for the feet, *svāhā*, sandalwood paste, unbroken rice, flowers, incense, and lamps— be completely fulfilled.

2a) The tasting with the *dhenumudrā*. Then, having performed the deception (*vañcana*), one should recite this mantra and cast the lamp outside: "Oṃ! Having performed the *nirāñjana*, I [perform] the destruction of sins with my foot. Be gracious, O Śrī Mahālakṣmī, who releases one from suffering and brings about happiness! For the sake of destroying all sins produced by sin and sinfulness, I perform this peace (*śānti*) which increases prosperity and brings blessings to men. Having spoken these words, one should cast the lamp outside. With the water from the *argha* vessel, one should sprinkle everything upon oneself.

Self-worship. Then, the worship of the gateway: Oṃ, obeisance to Nandin. Oṃ, obeisance to Mahākāla. Oṃ, obeisance to Gaṅgā. Oṃ, obeisance to Yamunā. Oṃ, obeisance to Dhātṛ. Oṃ, obeisance to Vidhātṛ. Oṃ, obeisance to Sarasvatī. Oṃ, obeisance to Mahālakṣmī. Oṃ, obeisance to Gomukha.

2b) Oṃ, homage to Hayamukha (the Horse-faced One). Oṃ, homage to Siṃhamukha (the Lion-faced One). Oṃ, homage to the Ṛgveda. Oṃ, homage to the Yajurveda. Oṃ, homage to the Sāmaveda. Oṃ, homage to the Atharvaveda. Oṃ, homage to the Kṛtayuga. Oṃ, homage to the Tretāyuga. Oṃ, homage to the Dvāparayuga. Oṃ, homage to the Kaliyuga. Oṃ, homage to Nandā. Oṃ, homage to Rudrā. Oṃ, homage to Jayā. Oṃ, homage to Riktā. Oṃ, homage to Parṇā. Oṃ.

Salutation to Saumyā. Oṃ, salutation to Bhīma. Oṃ, salutation to Mahābala. [Perform] the invocation and other rites. The procedure for the worship of the doors: Oṃ, salutation to Gaṇapati. Oṃ, salutation to Durgā. In the southeast (Āgneya): Oṃ, salutation to Vāyu. Oṃ, salutation to Guru. In the north (Uttara): Oṃ, salutation to Paramaguru. Oṃ, salutation to Parameṣṭhīguru. Oṃ.

Salutations to the Preceptor, the Ancient Teacher. Oṃ, salutations to the Guru, the Primordial Siddhi. In the center: Oṃ, salutations to Ādhāraśakti; Oṃ, salutations to Kūrmāmnāya; Oṃ, salutations to Anantāmnāya; Oṃ, salutations to Siṃhāmnāya; Oṃ, salutations to Dharmāmnāya; Oṃ, salutations to Jñānāmnāya; Oṃ, salutations to Vairājñāya; Oṃ, salutations to Aiśvarya; Oṃ, salutations to Adharma; Oṃ, salutations to Ajñāna; Oṃ, salutations to Vairājñāya; Oṃ, salutations to Anaiśvarya.
Homage! Oṃ, homage to Ardhacchanda. Oṃ, homage to Ūrdhvacchanda. Oṃ, homage to Kanda. Oṃ, homage to the Kaumārīmnāya.
3b) Meditation: In the state of youth and childhood, one meditates while seated upon a peacock throne.
The goddess wears a red color, her body as crimson as vermilion.
Resembling a barley flower, as radiant as a pomegranate blossom,
the goddess Tilocanā has one face and eyes like the petals of a blue lotus.
The goddess has four arms and possesses great heroism; she holds a spear, a trident, and a water-pot. The auspicious goddess holds a drinking vessel and a vessel for the *bindu*.
Goddess who wears various jewels, beautifully adorned with many gems;
Goddess who is the mistress of the three worlds, salutations to you, O you of universal form!
Oṃ, salutations again and again to the form of Kaumārī.
The invocations. The worship of Kālikā. The void.
Oṃ, salutation to the Padmāmnāya.
Oṃ, homage to Mahākāla.
Oṃ, salutation to the Vetālāmnāya. Meditation.
Oṃ! Seated upon a corpse-throne, Mahākālī is formidable;
she resembles a dark blue cloud, has one face and three eyes, four arms, a massive body, and is adorned with bone ornaments.
The auspicious Goddess has a face like a row of beautiful fangs, wears a hanging garland of severed heads,
carries a sword and a shield, and holds a vessel of *bindu*.
Adorned with ornaments of jewels, serpents, and bones, clothed in a tiger skin,
and always meditating upon the three worlds, Kālikā is the Yoginī of the universe.
Oṃ, salutation to the form of Mahākālī. [The rites of] invocation and so forth. Oṃ, salutation to the heart. Oṃ, salutation to the head.

Oṃ, salutation to the crest-lock (śikhā). Oṃ, salutation to the armor (kavaca). Oṃ, salutation to the eye (netra). Oṃ, salutation to the weapon (astra). Oṃ, salutation to Vāmā. Oṃ, salutation to Jyeṣṭhā. Oṃ, salutation to Raudrī. Oṃ, salutation to Kālī.

4b) Oṃ, homage to Kalavikarṇī! Oṃ, homage to Valapramathanī! Oṃ, homage to Sarvabhūtadamanī! [These are] up to the eastern direction. Worship of the filaments (*keśara*) and so forth: Oṃ, homage to Manonmanī! In the center: Oṃ, homage to Yayā! Oṃ, homage to Vijayā! Oṃ, homage to Ajitā! Oṃ, homage to Aparājitā! Oṃ, homage to Yamhanī! Oṃ, homage to Stambhanī! Oṃ, homage to Mohanī! Oṃ, homage to Ākarṣaṇī! [These are] at the tips of the filaments starting from the east. Oṃ...

In the second maṇḍala: Oṃ, homage to Brahmanī; Oṃ, homage to Māheśvarī; Oṃ, homage to Kaumārī; Oṃ, homage to Vaiṣṇavī; Oṃ, homage to Vārāhī; Oṃ, homage to Indrāyinī; Oṃ, homage to Cāmuṇḍā; Oṃ, homage to Mahālakṣmī. Then, in the third maṇḍala:
5a) Oṃ, homage to Devakī! Oṃ, homage to Susalī! Oṃ, homage to Viśalī! Oṃ, homage to Valāntakī! Oṃ, homage to Mālaṇī! Oṃ, homage to Ghorāmukhī! Oṃ, homage to Gavarī! Then, in the fourth maṇḍala:

Oṃ, homage to Rudracaṇḍa. Oṃ, homage to Caṇḍā. Oṃ, homage to Caṇḍavatī. Oṃ, homage to Caṇḍanāyikā. Oṃ, homage to Caṇḍā. Oṃ, homage to Caṇḍarūpā. Oṃ, homage to Caṇḍikā. In the center: Oṃ, homage to Ūrdhvacāṇḍā.

Then, in the fifth maṇḍala: Oṃ Viśveśvarī, homage! Oṃ Raudrī, homage! Oṃ Mahāraudrī, homage! Oṃ Viranāśikā, homage! Oṃ Drāvaṇī, homage! Oṃ Dravaṇī, homage! Oṃ Dharmaṇī, homage! Oṃ Kedaṇī, homage! Oṃ Dhūmraṇī, homage!
5b) Oṃ, homage to Dhūmravatī. Oṃ, homage to Krūrdhaṇī. Oṃ, homage to Marddaṇī. Oṃ, homage to Dhvaṃśinī. Oṃ, homage to Vidyujjihvā. Oṃ, homage to Dūrāntakī. Oṃ, homage to Vidyānta. [In the center.]

Then, in the seventh maṇḍala: Oṃ, obeisance to Valinī. Oṃ, obeisance to Ativali. Oṃ, obeisance to Bharanī. Oṃ, obeisance to Mahābharanī. Oṃ, obeisance to Grahani. Oṃ, obeisance to Mahāgrahani. Oṃ, obeisance to Atidaṃṣṭrā. Oṃ, obeisance to Mahādaṃṣṭrā.

Then, in the eighth maṇḍala: Oṃ Kalālī, homage! Oṃ Vikalālī, homage! Oṃ Mahākālī, homage! Oṃ Kapālī, homage! Oṃ Caurāgnī, homage! Oṃ Vaiṣvīyā, homage! Oṃ Lakṣmī, homage! Oṃ Mahālakṣmī, homage! Oṃ Mahāmāyā, homage! Oṃ Śrīmahālakṣmīmūrti, homage!

6a) In the center: Having worshipped [the deities] in the mandala beginning with the filaments (*keśara*), then in the center: *oṃ sarvalakṣmī namaḥ* | *oṃ viśvelakṣmī namaḥ* | *oṃ bhuvanalakṣmī namaḥ* | *oṃ rājyalakṣmī namaḥ* | *oṃ maṇḍalalakṣmī namaḥ* | *oṃ gṛhalakṣmī namaḥ* | *oṃ dhanalakṣmī namaḥ* | *oṃ dhānyalakṣmī namaḥ* | *oṃ santānalakṣmī namaḥ* | *oṃ jayalakṣmī namaḥ* | *oṃ vijayalakṣmī namaḥ* | *oṃ*...

Salutations to Khaḍgalakṣmī. Oṃ, salutations to Buddhilakṣmī. Oṃ, salutations to Dhṛtilakṣmī. Oṃ, salutations to Jñānalakṣmī. Oṃ, salutations to Mokṣalakṣmī. Oṃ, salutations to Mahālakṣmī. Oṃ, salutations to Ṣoḍaśalakṣmī. [Perform] the invocation and other rites. Oṃ, salutations to the one with a sword in hand. Oṃ, salutations to the one with a bell in hand. Oṃ, salutations to the one with arrows in hand.

6b) Oṃ, homage to the one with a thread in hand. Oṃ, homage to the one with a trident in hand. Oṃ, homage to the one with a lotus in hand. Oṃ, homage to the one with a goad in hand. Oṃ, homage to the one with a boon-granting hand. Oṃ, homage to the one with a *spheṭa* in hand. Oṃ, homage to the one with a *damaru* in hand. Oṃ, homage to the one with a bow in hand. Oṃ, homage to the one with a water-pot in hand. Oṃ, homage to the one with a skull-cup in hand. Oṃ, homage to the one with a book in hand. Oṃ, homage to the one with a noose in hand. Oṃ...
Homage to the one with the hand of fearlessness.

Thus ends the *śastra*. Oṃ, homage to Jayanātha. Oṃ, homage to Śrīnātha. Oṃ, homage to Siddhinātha. Oṃ, homage to Devanātha. Oṃ, homage to Yakṣanātha. Oṃ, homage to Asuranātha. Oṃ, homage to Nāganātha. Oṃ, homage to Vidyādharanātha. Oṃ, homage to Bhūtanātha.

7a) Oṃ, homage to the Lord of Pretas. Oṃ, homage to the Lord of Piśācas. Oṃ, homage to the Lord of Gurus. Oṃ, homage to the Lord of Rākṣasas. Oṃ, homage to the Lord of the Great Arena. Oṃ, homage to the Lord of Kinnaras. Oṃ, homage to the Lord of the Wheel of All Siddhis. Javasa. Oṃ, homage to Kaumārī. Oṃ, homage to her in the state of childhood. Oṃ, homage to the one of red color. Oṃ, homage to the one with a spear in hand. Oṃ, homage to the one with a thread in hand. Oṃ, homage to the one with a drop (bindu) in hand.

Homage! Oṃ, homage to the one with a vessel in hand. Oṃ, homage to Viśvarūpiṇī. Oṃ, [the rites] beginning with the invocation (āvāhana) and so forth. Khavasa. Oṃ, homage to Mahākāla. Oṃ, homage to Ghorāmukha. Oṃ, homage to the blue-colored one. Oṃ, homage to the one with a sword in hand.

7b) Oṃ, homage to the one with a sword in hand. Oṃ, homage to the one with a drop in hand. Oṃ, homage to the one with a vessel in hand. Oṃ, homage to Viśvayogin. Oṃ, [the rites of] invocation and so forth.

Oṃ, obeisance to Indra. Oṃ, obeisance to Agni. Oṃ, obeisance to Yama. Oṃ, obeisance to Nairṛti. Oṃ, obeisance to Varuṇa. Oṃ, obeisance to Vāyu. Oṃ, obeisance to Kuvera. Oṃ, obeisance to Īśāna. Oṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu. Oṃ, obeisance to Brahmā. Thus [ends] the World-Protectors. In the center of the *pūna*: Oṃ, obeisance to Goddess Brahmāṇī in Nepāla. Oṃ, obeisance to Goddess Māheśvarī in Prayāga. Oṃ, obeisance to Goddess Rākṣasī in Laṅkā. Oṃ, [obeisance to Goddess Kaumārī] in Kuntāla...
Salutation to the goddess Bhairavī. Oṃ, salutation to the goddess Jvālāmukhī of Jvālandhara. Oṃ, salutation to the goddess Kāmeśvarī, fierce in her desire.

8a) Oṃ, salutation to Sarasvatī of Kāśmīra. Oṃ, salutation to Viśvavyāpinī Mahālakṣmī. Oṃ, the mantra for invocation: Oṃ, Mahālakṣmī, come hither together with Padmanābha; for the sake of worship with the five offerings, this [place] has been prepared by me in various ways. Oṃ, the mantra for the seat: Oṃ, O Kamalālayā, here a lotus has been offered by me; O Goddess, O Kamalā, establish yourself within this lotus. Oṃ, O Viśvavyāpinī, Mother of the World!
O Mahālakṣmī, who brings about stability and consolidation, remain firm within my house just as you are! Homage to the Goddess Mahālakṣmī, the bestower of boons, the sovereign of the world!
Come, O auspicious one; take hold of this cause of suffering: *Oṃ*, [grant] sons, grandsons, and great-grandsons, and thereafter sons and grandsons.

8b) May my residence remain stable as long as the moon, sun, and earth endure. The mantra for the water for the feet (*pādya*): Oṃ! This water for the feet, which is the support of the waters of the Gaṅgā and other rivers, consecrated by the mantras of the sacred bathing sites (*tīrtha*), and which removes the exhaustion of traveling from afar—may you accept it. The mantra for the seat (*āsana*): Oṃ! Born upon the peak of the Himālaya mountain, pure and cool as the snowy mountains; this bath is offered to you. O Lakṣmī, salutations, salutations to you! The mantra for the garment (*vastra*): Oṃ...

There, [I offer] this sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*), joined with shoulder-straps, fashioned with skill in the arts, the most excellent ornament for all limbs, placed upon the broad chest, and fastened at the joint of the arm. Oṃ! O Goddess of the God of Gods, you whose form is the supreme seal of Brahman (*brahmamudrā*), please accept this sixteen-stranded, complete sacred thread. Sandalwood:
Oṃ! [This sandalwood paste], produced on the Malaya mountain, protected by various cities, and filled with fragrance...

9a) Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Mahālakṣmī. On the eighth day of the bright fortnight of Bhādrapada: as before, the Brahmin performs the offering of arghya to the Sun; [then follows] the ritual placement (nyāsa).

The worship of the broken vessel (*khughapātra*). The worship of the Self (*ātmā-pūjā*). The seat (*āsana*). The *tatvājām* mantra and so forth. *Oṃ jātavedase*. *Oṃ aṃbe aṃvike*. *Oṃ śvrīśyate*. *Oṃ ākṛne*.

*Trātālam indra*. *Oṃ abhyantaro*. *Oṃ ardhamāsāḥ*. *Saṃlasa*. The jar (*kalaśa*). Gaṇapati. The morsel (*gegrāsa*). Komali. Vari. The fourfold worship of the Vedas (*kevovedārcana catusvati*). Incense, lamps, betel-leaf, and consecration (*pratiṣṭhā*). Recitation (*jāpa*) and hymns (*stotra*). The offering of perfumes and other items (*trātragaṃdhādi*). Therein, in the religious gift (*dharmadānaka*), the Goddess [is worshipped] according to the *jayā* ritual.

Having worshipped with sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, and so forth; having performed the recitation (*jāpa*), hymns of praise (*stotra*), and other rites, and having paid obeisance; then, taking up sixteen bone-threads (*asthisūtra*) placed before the Goddess in a number of sixteen.

9b) Oṃ ṣoḍaśāni ca. Oṃ jayajayarameśvarī kamaraṃkama-reśvarī kamaramaho māhārarkṣya rājyamede svāhā. With this mantra, one should recite it for each knot. Having recited "Oṃ pravidvyartha," one should wear [the cord] on the right arm; for women, on the left. Then, holding a handful of flowers, one should make this request: having recited "Oṃ adyaprabhṛti" (from today onwards), and having paid obeisance, one should perform the dismissal according to the ritual with the mantra. Thus.

The Procedure for Observing the Mahālakṣmī Vow || 0 || Now, having prepared the offerings for worship on the eighth day of the dark fortnight (Kṛṣṇāṣṭamī), one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as previously described: *oṃ mahālakṣmī astrāya namaḥ*; *oṃ mahālakṣmyai hṛdayāya namaḥ* (twice); *oṃ mahālakṣmyai śirase namaḥ* (twice).

10a) Oṃ, salutation to the head of Mahālakṣmī (twice). Oṃ, salutation to the armor of Mahālakṣmī (twice). Oṃ, salutation to the eyes of Mahālakṣmī (twice). Oṃ, salutation to the weapon of Mahālakṣmī (twice). Worship of the Argha vessel. Self-worship. Oṃ, to Gaṇapati (twice). Oṃ, to Gulurbha (twice). Oṃ, to Nandin (twice). Oṃ, to Mahākāla (twice). To Gaṅgā (twice). Oṃ, to Yamunā (twice). Oṃ, to Caṇḍa (twice). Oṃ, to Pracaṇḍa (twice). Oṃ, to Gemuṣā (twice). Oṃ, to Hayamuṣā. Oṃ...

The Siṃhacakra: Oṃ vārāha mūṣāyai 2. Oṃ ādhāraśaktaye 2. Oṃ anantāsanāya 2. Oṃ kolopurī-mahāpīṭhāsanāya 2. Oṃ padmāya 2. Oṃ keśavāya 2. Oṃ karṇikāya 2. Oṃ mahālakṣmī-āsanaṃ 2. Oṃ mahālakṣmyai 2. Oṃ mahālakṣmī 2.
Having offered a single oblation of flowers with the mantra "Victory! Victory! and so forth.
10b) Again, the worship of the heart and so forth: Then, having taken flour and placed a lamp in its center, one takes a mustard seed.

Oṃ mahālakṣmī astrāya 2 || Oṃ, for the destruction of all sins—sinful ones, sinful things, and the ashes of sin—I perform this which brings about the increase of Lakṣmī and bestows blessings; [thus] I cause [the flour] to go forth. One should cast the flour outside the enclosure. Having performed the nyāsa and other rites as before, and having worshipped the guardians of the gates and so forth, one should worship Mahākālī upon the maṇḍala of the Goddess. Oṃ ādhāraśaktaye 2 || Oṃ anantāsanāya 2 || Oṃ prītāsanāya 2 || Oṃ padmāya 2 || Oṃ keśarāya 2 || Oṃ...
At the pericarp: oṃ kāli 2 || oṃ mahākāli 2 || oṃ arśicarmāhastāya 2 ||

11a) Oṃ vetārāsnāya 2 || Oṃ gholāmukhī 2 || Oṃ ūrddhakesāya 2 || Oṃ mahākālyāsnāya || Meditation (Dhyāna): Oṃ! She whose face is beautiful and free from impurity, who increases the [offering of] human heads; the Goddess who wears a garland of skulls and possesses a skull-cup and a khaṭvāṅga staff; she who has a serpent as her sacred thread and moves upon a corpse as her vehicle; she who is endowed with the mudrā, the vessel, and the cause of the trident; she whose color is like that of wine and who is meditated upon as blue—[I] worship her. Oṃ.

Ham Mahākālyai 2 || 3 || Worship of the Heart and other limbs (hṛdayādipūjā). Having performed the invocation (āvāhana) and so forth, as well as the offering of sandalwood paste (candana), unbroken rice grains (akṣata), flowers (puṣpa), incense (dhūpa), lamps (dīpa), food offerings (naivedya), and so on, [one performs] the recitation (jāpa) together with the mantra. Having paid obeisance, [one worships] the goddess on the left side; this is the worship of Kumārī (komālipūjā).

11b) Oṃ ādhāla saktaya 2 || Oṃ anaṃtāsnāya 2 || Oṃ mayūlāsasnāya 2 || Oṃ padmaya 2 || Oṃ keśarāya 2 || Oṃ kaṇṇikāya 2 || Oṃ kaumārī 2 || Oṃ śaktihastāya 2 || Oṃ mayūravāhanāya 2 || Oṃ sainyādhipataya 2 || Oṃ kṛśānudīptāya 2 || Oṃ guhyaśva 2 || Oṃ lohitavarṇāya 2 || Oṃ rāmeśvarī 2 || Oṃ kaumālyāsnāya 2 || Meditation (Dhyāna): Oṃ, she whose limbs are red like the color of vermilion, [like] the Āimī flower...

Prabhā: The goddess has three eyes and four arms; she holds a spear and a rosary in her hands. With two hands she displays the *mudrā* and holds a vessel. Adorned with various ornaments, she is seated upon Nīlakaṇṭha and possesses all auspicious limbs and features. Having meditated thus, O Kumārī, one should worship her with this prayer.

12a) Oṃ hrīḥ kaumāryai 2 || 3 || Having offered sandalwood paste, unbroken rice, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, and so forth for the worship of the heart and other limbs, [one should perform] the recitation and the hymn of praise.

Having paid homage, one should then worship Mahālakṣmī in the center: Oṃ, to Vibhūti, twice. Oṃ, to the great seat (pīṭha) of Kolāpuri, twice. Oṃ, to Ādhāraśakti, twice. Oṃ, to Anantāsana, twice. Oṃ, to the lotus (padma), twice. Oṃ, to the filaments (keśara), twice. Oṃ, to the pericarp (karṇikā), twice. Oṃ, to the seat of Mahālakṣmī, twice. [With this] meditation: Oṃ, her limbs radiant with a golden hue, three-eyed, riding upon a lion; the Goddess is slightly smiling, with eyes like blue lotus petals, adorned with fourteen arms.
Adorned with all ornaments, she holds a sword, a bell, a lotus thread, a trident, and a lotus.

12b) O you who hold a flame in your right hand, O bestower of boons, O swift giver of gifts! Likewise, with your left hand, [you hold] a *phetaka* (noose), a *ḍiṇḍima* (drum), a bow, a water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*), a skull-cup (*kapāla*), a book, and the gesture of fearlessness (*abhaya*). O you who are ablaze, burning with splendors that surpass even fire! Having meditated thus with diligence, one should then worship the Goddess. [This is] the three-fold *añjali*. 3. 16a) Three handfuls [of water]. 3. [Offering] to the heart and other limbs. Bathing: Oṃ, I bathe you with the purifying waters of all holy places, such as the Gaṅgā and the seven celestial rivers, whose waters have been drawn forth by the gods. Sandalwood paste: Oṃ, divine Śrīkhaṇḍa sandalwood, ancient and praised of old, obtained according to my desire; be gracious, O Supreme Goddess. Be gracious. [For the] garment: O Goddess, [I offer] this garment adorned with various cloths for the gods, as long as the thread remains upon the body of the one who knows the truth.
[For the] sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*): *Oṃ*. O Mistress of the Gods, you who are the form of the joy of Brahmā, please accept this sacred thread, complete with sixteen strands.

16b) Ṣoḍaśapuṣpa: Endowed with sixteen varieties, I offer this flower-garland and so forth. O Mistress of the World, please accept this which has been given by me for the sake of worship. Tulasī: The purifier of the three worlds, the beloved of Hari, the source of pilgrimage for the universe—O Tulasī, please accept [this].

**Jātī Flower:** Among all varieties of *jātī* flowers, the white *jātī* is praised. By the offering of *jātī* flowers, one rejoices together with the Gandharvas. **Lotus (Padma):** The lotus is like the essence of the milk-ocean. O Lotus-flower, you who are held by the supreme Lakṣmī; Great Lakṣmī resides within you. Homage to you, O Lotus-flower! **Blue Lotus (Utpala):** The blue lotus petal is a flower exceedingly difficult to obtain. Having meditated thus upon the blue lotus...

Then the Goddess accepts the *uphola* [offering]. O Dūrvā grass, you who are the time of the Dūrvā, the flower that is the most excellent among all flowers; together with the sixteen *akṣatas*, O Mahālakṣmī, bestower of happiness, just as the branches spread forth and as the Dūrvā grows, so may there be an increase in my lineage and prosperity—accept this, O Mistress! O Damana, you who arise from the body of Madana, the purifier of those who are already pure, O Mahālakṣmī...
